- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., +1.00) followed by a spike, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After strong negative sentiment shifts (e.g., -1.00), model underreacts — increase forecast by 3–7% to avoid mean reversion lag.
- If sentiment change is volatile (±0.67+), model exhibits lag — forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% for each 0.33 sentiment change.
- When news volume drops to 0 for 1–2 days, model underperforms — add 2–5% bias to forecast to compensate for reduced market noise.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 2–4% to forecast if sentiment < 0.67.
- If model forecast is > 10% above true outcome, check for sentiment spike — if sentiment was positive 3+ days ago, reduce forecast by 5–8% to avoid overcorrection.
- If true outcome is > 10% above model, sentiment was likely negative 2–3 days ago — model is lagging — increase forecast by 3–6% to catch momentum.
